description:
FILED s421 (Fable, while reviewing s422/#419).  perl prints 67108864 for all three.

  chr1.pl:  my $c = chr(0x4000000); print ord($c), "\n";
            PCL default 65533 | PCL_OPT=none 67108864
  chr3.pl:  my $c = chr(0x4000000); print ord($c), "\n"; print length($c), "\n";
            PCL default 65533 1 | PCL_OPT=none 67108864 1
  chr2.pl:  print "start\n"; my $c = chr(0x4000000); print ord($c), "\n";
            my $s = "abc"; eval { $s =~ s/b/x/ }; print "end\n";
            PCL default 67108864 (!)  | PCL_OPT=none 67108864

Emission for chr1: (let (($c (%pcl-to-string-strict (p-chr #x4000000) "$c"))) ...)
— a raw-string slot verdict; the boxed path (PCL_OPT=none, or chr2 where the
verdict differs) keeps the number.  So the s318 §11 ruling (chr of an
unrepresentable code point yields U+FFFD, op/chr.t 40-42 registered XDIFF) is
applied by ONE coercion path and not the other: two answers for one value,
chosen by an optimizer verdict.  Related: docs/fable-answers-s422-s424.md §A
(the literal → die asymmetry was RATIFIED with this as the recorded caveat).
Fix direction: whichever answer s318 §11 means, %pcl-to-string-strict and the
boxed to-string must agree — probe both, then one place.  0 corpus rows.

CLOSED s427 (Opus).  MEASURED FIRST, both paths, nine shapes vs perl 5.40.3:
the GENERAL-FORM compiler (PCL_OPT=none) was already right on all nine —
ord(chr(N)), the assigned copy, a further copy, array and hash elements,
chr(0x110000), chr(-1), chr(0x10FFFF).  Only the DEFAULT emission diverged,
and only where the scalar took the raw-string slot verdict.  So the bug
belonged to the OPTIMIZATION, not to the s318 §11 ruling, and it is what the
optimization registry forbids in so many words: the optimized emission must
RUN identically to the general form.

FIX: %pcl-to-string-strict called to-string on the p-superchar payload,
pre-empting a decision the general path makes later.  It now passes a
superchar through (%pcl-superchar-payload), so the U+FFFD collapse happens at
to-string, where the boxed path makes it, and nowhere earlier.  The predicate
looks through a plain box but deliberately NOT through unbox's tie/magic
dispatch — a proxy is never a superchar and FETCH would run twice for one
write.  The first cut missed the box entirely (`my $d = $c` still answered
65533); the 15-shape probe caught it, the task's reproducer did not.

Both emissions are now IDENTICAL on 15 shapes (length, ord, interpolation, uc,
eq self, eq "\x{FFFD}", hash key, concat, substr, boolean, index, copy, .=
append, split, sprintf) and match perl on every row where the CHARACTER itself
is not consumed.  docs/not-supported.md corrected: s422's "once the value has
been assigned it is 65533" recorded the bug as the rule.  Guard
Pl/t/wide-codepoint-01.t rows 8-11 (including the both-emissions row that IS
the property).  Generation v2-173 (the assigned v2-171 collided with agent B's tree and the
shared ~/.pcl-cache is keyed by it, so the branch moved to a fresh string and
re-ran the gate and the sweep under it; both agreed row for row).  Full sweep
GATE clean, TOTAL 18365 (+0).
title: chr(N) for N > 0x10FFFF answers 65533 or 67108864 depending on the OPTIMIZER verdict and the surrounding statements (s318 §11 blessed U+FFFD is not uniformly applied)
